text:
alex: Heads up — eu-west3 is seeing repeated GPU attach failures over the last 10m. Early correlation points to massive local NVMe metadata checkpoint bursts causing IOPS saturation and write stalls. Logs below.

alex: ```
kernel: nvme0: write stall detected, qdepth=128, ops_in_flight=64
checkpointd[1123]: flushed 12034 metadata entries in 0.9s
provisioner: attach failed: timeout waiting for disk ready (err=EIO)
system: iostat -x shows nvme0 util=99% avgqu-sz=45
```

maya: Oof. Any idea what triggered the checkpoint flood? region-wide or per-node?

alex: Looks region-wide but starts near 12:03 UTC. Spike matches model-sync job and a chunked replica reconcile from apac -> eu-west3.

devin: Can we throttle checkpointd or make it cooperative with IO scheduler? If we push metadata writes into short windows they thrash the NVMe metadata journal.

sre-bot: alert: gpu-attach-failure-eu-west3 count=27 severity=high

maya: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) reduce concurrent model-sync workers 2) flip checkpointd to background mode 3) move some attaches off this pool. Which is fastest?

alex: Fast path: throttle checkpointd via feature flag (rate-limit meta ops), and change scheduler on a canary node: `echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler` — that reduced write-latency jitter in past incidents.

ops-junior: I applied the scheduler change to gnode-eu-194 (canary). Attach success rate improved immediately. Logs: "attach ok" for 12/12 attempted GPUs in the last 120s.

devin: Good. For the flag we can add CLI opts: `--meta-qps=500 --meta-backoff-ms=100`. Also add metrics: meta_ops/sec and meta_flush_latency_bucketed.

maya: Rolling a quick feature-flag deploy to eu-west3 canary pool now. Will also throttle model-sync from 10 -> 3 concurrent workers.

alex: Decision: Do emergency mitigations now (throttle + scheduler + divert low-prio batch). Follow-ups: post-incident triage for long-term fixes (separate meta SSD class, cooperative checkpointing, smarter batching).

sre-bot: incident-bot: incident created INC-2026-1347 (priority P1)

devin: Long-term note: write amplification here is metadata-driven. We should consider: bigger in-memory metadata caches, batched metadata flush windows that respect IO headroom, or separating metadata onto a different storage tier. Cost tradeoff: dedicated metadata SSDs adds ~$0.02/node/hr but reduces attach failure risk.

ops-junior: I pushed a small rate-limiter patch to checkpointd (`rate_limit_meta_ops`) and wired up prometheus metric `checkpointd_meta_qps`. Deploying to canary now.

maya: Rolling to 30% of eu-west3 pool. Monitoring latency, attach failures and nvme util.

alex: Monitoring dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/storage/eu-west3 (watching meta_qps, nvme_util, gpu_attach_fail_rate). Will update after 10m.

ops-junior: Canary looks stable so far. nvme util dropped from ~98% -> ~60% and attach failures stopped.

maya: :thumbsup: continuing slow rollout. planning postmortem and backlog item `storage/metadata-burst-mitigation`.

devin: Adding an action item: test isolating metadata writes to separate pool in staging (cost estimate + runbook).

alex: Thanks everyone — Maya + Devin own the mitigation rollout. Ops-junior will run follow-up verification scripts and add metrics alerts. I'll file the incident and schedule a triage tomorrow.

maya: Updating incident with timeline and canary evidence.

ops-junior: Patch merged to checkpointd main (rate limiter + metrics). Deploying to remaining eu-west3 nodes as of now.

alex: Closing thread for now. Postmortem draft when we have 24h of stable telemetry.
